title: Movie booking lifecycle
idea: The booking lifecycle is a small state machine: a Booking starts PENDING and may only move along allowed arrows to CONFIRMED, EXPIRED or CANCELLED.
points: PENDING moves to CONFIRMED on payment, EXPIRED on timeout, or CANCELLED.
CONFIRMED can only become CANCELLED; EXPIRED and CANCELLED are final.
Seats go AVAILABLE, HELD, BOOKED; expiry or cancel returns them to AVAILABLE.
An illegal move is refused in one place, not checked in every caller.

messages.label: hold(SH-1, [A2, P1])
messages.note: The customer picks two seats and asks to hold them.

messages.label: lockAll(seats, H-1)
messages.note: All seats lock together or none do. Seats move AVAILABLE to HELD.

messages.label: H-1, expires 18:10
messages.note: The customer gets a hold id and a deadline to show as a timer.

messages.label: confirm(H-1, token)
messages.note: Checkout starts. A PENDING Booking is created; page 3 skipped this step for brevity.

messages.label: charge(total)
messages.note: The service prices the seats and charges the total once.

messages.label: ok
messages.note: Payment succeeded, so the Booking moves PENDING to CONFIRMED.

messages.label: markBooked(H-1)
messages.note: The held seats become BOOKED. This adds a markBooked method to the SeatLockProvider interface from page 3.

messages.label: BK-1 CONFIRMED
messages.note: If the hold had expired first, the Booking would be EXPIRED instead.

code.title: Status enum with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. Booking asks the enum before changing state.

walk.text: BK-1 takes the happy path, then the customer cancels it.
BK-2 expires, then a late payment tries to confirm it.
An `EnumMap` lists the allowed next states for each state.
`canMoveTo` is the single question every transition asks.
Refuse and report an illegal move; otherwise record the new state.

pitfalls: Do not set `status` directly from controllers; every change goes through `moveTo`.
A late payment for an EXPIRED booking needs a refund, not a silent confirm.
Keep seat state and booking state separate; they change for different reasons.

quiz.q: What does the last line of BookingLifecycle print?
quiz.why: EXPIRED has no allowed next states, so `canMoveTo(CONFIRMED)` is false and `moveTo` prints the refusal without changing status.

takeaway: Write allowed transitions once, in the enum, and refuse everything else.

starters: Should a booking have a PAYMENT_FAILED state?
How do I handle a payment that succeeds after the hold expired?
Would the State pattern be better than an enum here?
